A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same MBOK research work and include Appendices A–J. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison of the methods, equations, proofs, tables, and figures across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original MBOK perplexity, zero-shot accuracy, optimization, and latency results in Section 6 and Appendix G, alongside comparator results attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds distillation and initialization ablations, scaling-distribution analysis, and training-convergence results in Appendices G.7–G.10.

M1.justification: The multiple Boolean kernels, successive SVID initialization, Boolean optimizer, last-kernel finetuning, distillation objectives, and kernel-allocation procedure are retained. The new training variants appear only as ablation controls.

E1.justification: WikiText2/C4 language modeling, the existing zero-shot tasks, and generation examples are retained without new datasets or task requirements. The added OPT-30B convergence curves extend model-size evaluation within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Figures 13 and 16 add internal comparison variants: training without knowledge distillation and random initialization. External benchmark comparator membership is unchanged; GPTQ/OPTQ denotes the same Frantar et al. method, and QUIP#/QTIP comparisons already appeared in v2.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce two-kernel OPT-125M controls, a four-kernel first-layer scaling-distribution comparison, and three-kernel convergence evaluation through OPT-30B. The existing training recipe and appendix latency protocol are retained; the changed Table 3 scores are not accompanied by a stated protocol revision.

E4.justification: v2 already studies kernel count, which kernels to optimize, and distillation-loss choice. v3 substantially extends this analysis with direct KD/no-KD and SVID/random-initialization ablations, before/after scaling distributions, and convergence diagnostics across OPT sizes (Figures 13–16).

E5.justification: Figure 14 newly reports Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistics and kernel density estimates comparing scaling distributions before and after finetuning. These add statistical characterization; additional repeated runs, confidence intervals, or significance tests are not documented.

E6.justification: Table 3 substantially replaces RTN and GPTQ/OPTQ scores under unchanged stated bit widths. For OPT-2.7B WikiText2, GPTQ/OPTQ changes from 12.87 to 16.88 while MBOK remains 13.09, reversing their ranking. Figures 13–16 also add no-KD/random-initialization outcomes, scaling statistics, and convergence curves. The latency values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The Boolean-variation definitions and calculus, SVID propositions and proofs, kernel-allocation formulation, and training-complexity derivation are retained. The new empirical KS analysis introduces no new formal definition, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about direct Boolean finetuning, successive knowledge transfer, flexible kernel allocation, and accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. The expanded latency discussion reiterates claims already present in v2's appendix.

C2.justification: New discussion interprets higher flipping rates with KD as more effective teacher-guided learning and concentrated changes in the last kernel's scaling values as support for retaining lower-order initialization. Random-initialization behavior receives additional interpretation. The stated hardware limitation is unchanged.

D1.justification: The latency environment becomes slightly less specific: v2 identifies a Google Cloud A100 GPU, whereas v3 states only A100. Core implementation samples, training hyperparameters, V100 hardware disclosure, and implementation links are retained; no hardware change is established.

R1.justification: Table 1 changes BiLLM's classification for higher-bit salient weights from no to yes, refining its characterization relative to MBOK. The bibliography and broader research positioning are unchanged; GPTQ-to-OPTQ naming does not introduce a different cited work.

P1.justification: v3 adds four short experimental appendix subsections and expands Section 6.6's latency discussion while preserving the overall narrative and most prose. Other edits include baseline naming, affiliation, publication headers, and cross-references.

P2.justification: v3 adds four substantial multipanel analytical figures (13–16), enlarges Figure 4, and adjusts spacing and page flow. New main-text Table 4 redisplays v2's appendix latency Table 12, also retained as v3 Table 13; it is not new latency evidence.

improvement.justification: The new KD/no-KD and SVID/random-initialization controls fill a useful validation gap, while scaling and convergence diagnostics strengthen the optimization analysis. These are incremental gains over v2's already extensive evidence. The large, unexplained Table 3 baseline-score revisions limit confidence in the revised comparison margins.
